# Port the real slice to Phrase in the private folder

- **Status:** Superseded 2026-10-27 by cards 125 and 126 (Decider D84): Steve dropped the private projects in favour of a public repository
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (thin slice; a private port)
- **Milestone:** Codebase size: does Phrase's cost fall and its edge widen as the codebase grows?
- **Source:** Steve's idea relayed by Dispatch, 2026-10-27 (test against different code base sizes; use his real projects as the medium and large codebases) and Decider D82 (Codex, Grok Support-it; Copilot Yes). A separate question beside the frozen bar (D32); no frozen number changes and no stored row is re-scored.
- **Depends on:** 121
- **Story:** As Ari, I want the scrubbed slice written in Phrase beside its C# original, so that a modify or fix task on real code can be given in both languages.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given the scrubbed slice, When the mob writes the Phrase version, Then it compiles with the C# adapter and its generated specs pass the same outcome cases as the C# original's tests, with native csharp blocks only where Phrase has no vocabulary (counted and reported as a total)
  2. Given the two versions, When modify and fix tasks are chosen, Then each needs context from another file in the slice and is recorded in the pre-registered task list before any run
  3. Given the port, When the repository checks run, Then nothing from it is tracked

## Context

- REAL-PROJECT RULES (binding, D82): read-only (never modify, commit, branch or run anything in the source project; take a snapshot copy only, by the facilitator, only after Dispatch confirms the exact source folder in chat); the copy is source files only (no git history, databases, logs or secret files) in a git-ignored folder like the holdouts; secrets (connection strings, keys, production endpoints, user data) are scrubbed before any author reads it, by an automated scan plus a manual check recorded in a scrub manifest; Dispatch accepts in chat that the scrubbed slice is sent to the model CLIs (external providers); nothing from the project (code, data, names, paths, prompts, replies) is ever committed; only totals are published; rows go to private results (cards 113 and 114); a retention rule deletes the copy when the experiment ends.
- Whether a slice is enough instead of a full port is settled by D82: a slice.
